title: a proof that writes a record fixture the artifact door later reads writes it through the scratch tool's LF writer
intention: The scratch tool publishes write_fixture(path, text), which writes text-mode fixtures with newline="\n"; its sieve fixture_writes_without_lf(root) names every proof under root that makes a text-mode write without newline= in a file that also reaches the artifact door (write_ticket, rewrite_ticket, write_state, cast_ticket, door/artifact write, emit, clear); the migrated proofs use the writer and the sieve reads empty.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on Windows: a fixture plan written by Path.write_text gets CRLF, and the artifact door's byte round-trip (ticket_file.ticket_shape: the ticket's serialisation cannot be reproduced) refuses it, so the proof reds on Windows only (test_a_hand_kick_back_writes_the_fixme_list). The orchestrator ruled the door stays strict (it protects a record of truth) and the fix is at the writer. Static census of origin/main, 746 proof files: 1369 text-mode writes lack newline=, but only 26 files (83 record-looking writes) also reach the door, so the migration is 26 files, not ~190.
traces_to: Law 4 (a fixture written LF becomes a sieve, not a habit), Law 3 (the count is the sieve's, a measurement), Law 8 (a proof is the same proof on every box).
how: D1 add write_fixture to scratch.py. D2 add the sieve beside bare_temp_reach/scratch_home_bypass (same stance: public, names no caller, exempts nothing). D3 one proof, one tooth per clause. D4 migrate the 26 files by replacing X.write_text(S, encoding=E) with write_fixture(X, S) (mechanical AST edit; the sieve reading empty is the check). Red-first: the sieve over origin/main's pre-migration tree names the files; the writer's output has no CR on Windows.

clauses.claim: write_fixture(path, text) writes bytes with no CR on every host, for text with and without newlines, and creates nothing else

fixture_writes_without_lf over a scratch tree holding one proof with a record write lacking newline= beside a write_ticket call names that proof's line; the same proof written with write_fixture, or with newline="\n", or with no door call in the file, names nothing
fixture_writes_without_lf over the repo's real tree names nothing (the migration is complete), except files an open ticket still owns, named in the proof's own list

decisions.text: D1: write_fixture in the scratch tool; a tool's published function, no other component imported.

D2: the sieve in the same file, over proofs/test_*.py, AST-based, per file: a text-mode write (write_text or open('w') lacking newline=) whose target text is record-looking AND the file calls a door-reaching name. Measured over origin/main: 27 files / 83 writes (26 after excluding the LF-fixture proof).
D3: the one proof, one tooth per clause.

D4: migrate exactly the sieve's files to write_fixture; read-only fixtures stay so seals re-red only where the bug is. Files that overlap other open tickets (test_transitions.py, test_a_fixme_answer_binds_to_its_kick_back.py, test_every_watching_class_can_fixme.py, test_fixme.py) land after those tickets, or I rebase.

out: every proof not named in the sieve's list

measured.saw: 1369 text-mode writes without newline= in 746 proof files (645 record-looking); of those, 83 record-looking writes in 27 files sit in a file that also calls a door-reaching name; direct arg-match tier 0, same-function tier 11 writes in 10 files
measured.how: static AST census over git show origin/main (scratchpad census_lf.py, census_door.py, census_door2.py)

measured.saw: UNMEASURED: how many of the 27 files actually red on Windows. The sieve's count is a same-file upper bound; per the orchestrator no Windows run is made for it.
